q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

problems: figures in no tool result and not one arithmetic step from them: 28.1%

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
Short answer — the premise is off: ROAS rose, but net profit did not fall; it improved (became less negative). The rise in ROAS is arithmetic: ad spend fell by more than sales did, so sales ÷ spend (ROAS) went up even though contribution dropped.

Compact evidence (previous → current; previous first)
- Periods: 2026-08-14..2026-09-12 → 2026-09-13..2026-10-12 (Measured)
- Net sales: ₹2,998,018 → ₹1,830,381 (Measured)  
- Ad spend (paid): ₹2,144,355 → ₹1,022,152 (Measured)  
- Gross ROAS (net_sales ÷ ad_spend): 1.4x → 1.8x — change +28.1% (Derived from measured inputs)  
- Contribution margin: ₹1,574,718 → ₹981,473 (Measured)  
- Net profit: ₹-569,638 → ₹-40,679 (Measured)

What this means (labels)
- Measured: ROAS increased because the denominator (ad spend) dropped proportionally more than net sales.  
- Measured: Contribution margin fell in absolute terms, which works against profit.  
- Measured identity (accounting): net_profit = contribution_margin − order_pnl_ad_spend. In these periods the ad‑spend reduction outweighed the contribution drop, so net_profit improved overall. (Measured / Derived)

Note / next step (Hypothesis)
